changes.rationale: November 25 release announces acquisition of Healthland, and contemporaneous market coverage links CPSI gains to that announcement. CPSI is the buyer. METHODOLOGY section 9 class-2 note permits acquirer news when reviewed as the attributed jump cause; retain acquirer role explicitly.

March 30 Hyperion filing documents Horizon acquisition terms. Contemporaneous market coverage links Horizon gains to the deal. Horizon is the buyer; apply the explicit class-2 acquirer exception in METHODOLOGY section 9, not a target-takeover label.

October 21 issuer release announces the Clarient acquisition and an 11 a.m. ET transaction call. Retain existing acquisition-led jump attribution; NEO is explicitly the buyer, qualifying under METHODOLOGY section 9 acquirer exception. GE receiving stock is transaction consideration rather than a standalone financing catalyst.
June 5 issuer release reports Q2 revenues, volumes, margins and EPS. Retain earnings exclusion despite positive operating headline.

Recurrent acquisition could qualify under the class-2 acquirer exception, but issuer page and later financial release identify February 2 announcement while Sharp notice is February 3. Exact public-release timing is unresolved for February 3 reaction; defer rather than assign a same-session keep.

Standalone 2015 budget and roughly 50% year-over-year production-growth outlook could fit class 8, but primary release is December 8. Exact announcement time and novelty relative to prior outlook are unresolved for December 9 jump.

July 25 release authorizes pursuit of ONE Gas spin-off and schedules a July 26 call. Strategic separation could fit class 11, but exact release time and attribution to July 25 rather than July 26 need verification. Do not conflate a future separation plan with a mechanical ex-distribution print.

March 30 filing confirms Lincoln Continental Concept used SPD-SmartGlass. A concept-car showcase alone does not establish a material commercial order or production launch. Defer class 5/10 eligibility pending evidence of commercialization rather than treat marketing language as a technical breakthrough.
